correctness.rationale: For all prime powers, complement duality reduces to k≤n/2. The explicit common-complement lemma realizes the nonadjacent-to-both pattern for every pair when k≥2. Dimension-one and dimension-two pairs admit all four adjacency patterns; the n=4,k=2 boundary is handled by a separate linear combination. Triangle inequality forbids a common neighbor exactly at distance≥3, while remaining profiles still occur. This supplies a three-move EF strategy for each class and rank-three separators between classes, plus Gaussian-binomial minimum witness proofs. checker.py exhaustively verifies representative binary and ternary profiles; no finite check is mistaken for an all-field proof.

value.rationale: A very recent primary paper explicitly proposes model-theoretic treatment of finite-field PGJ as a natural question. The four-class rank-three theorem is a complete all-field bounded-depth logical classification, with a sharp Rado agreement boundary, a complete pair-witness structure and optimal family-internal representatives of orders 35 and 1395. These are motivated exact invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices; no full limit-theory claim is made.
